results.question: During a registration procedure, if the AMF determines that the maximum number of UEs has been reached for all S-NSSAIs in the requested NSSAI and there are no default S-NSSAIs which can be allowed, what action does the AMF take and which message does it use?
results.reference: The AMF includes the rejected NSSAI accordingly in the REGISTRATION REJECT message as specified in subclauses 5.5.1.2.5 and 5.5.1.3.5.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 4.6.2.5, Mobility management based network slice admission control; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.1.3.5, Mobility and periodic registration update not accepted by the network
results.model_answer: The AMF rejects the registration and sends a REGISTRATION REJECT message with 5GMM cause #62, "No network slices available."
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (UE-initiated registration procedure / AMF handling of requested NSSAI): when the maximum UE limit is reached for all requested S-NSSAIs and no default S-NSSAI can be allowed, the AMF sends REGISTRATION REJECT with cause #62.

results.question: What action does the UE take upon receiving a SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message, and what is the purpose of the overall procedure?
results.reference: Upon receipt of a SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMMAND message, the UE passes to the upper layers the service-level-AA payload received in the Service-level-AA container IE. The purpose of the service-level authentication and authorization procedure is to enable the DN to authenticate and/or authorize the upper layers of the UE when establishing or after establishing a PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.1A.2, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 6.3.1A, Service-level authentication and authorization procedure
results.model_answer: The UE performs the requested service-level authentication, using the indicated service credentials/authentication data, and returns the result/authentication response in a SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMPLETE message. The procedure is used to authenticate/authorize the UE for the specific service and to establish the corresponding service-level authentication context.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.6 (Service level authentication procedure), especially clause 5.4.6.2 (service-level authentication initiated by the network / UE handling of SERVICE-LEVEL AUTHENTICATION COMMAND).

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE include the Ethernet header compression configuration IE in a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message, and when may the SMF subsequently include it in the response?
results.reference: The UE shall include the Ethernet header compression configuration IE if the PDU session type is set to "Ethernet", the UE indicated support for "Control Plane CIoT 5GS optimization" and "Ethernet header compression for control plane CIoT 5GS optimization" in the REGISTRATION REQUEST, and the network indicated the same support in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT (Clause_8_3_1_14). The SMF may include the Ethernet header compression configuration IE in the response if the network accepts an Ethernet PDU session type, control plane CIoT 5GS optimization is selected, and the UE provided the Ethernet header compression configuration IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message (Clause_8_3_2_18).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.1.14, Ethernet header compression configuration; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.2.18, Ethernet header compression configuration
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the Ethernet header compression configuration IE in a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST when it requests an Ethernet PDU session and wants to use Ethernet header compression (i.e. the UE supports Ethernet header compression and requests its use for that session). The SMF may include the IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT when Ethernet header compression is accepted/selected for the PDU session, to provide the negotiated Ethernet header-compression configuration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.2 (PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST) and clause 6.4.1.3 (PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT), including the Ethernet header compression configuration IE presence/handling requirements; IE definition in clause 9.11 (Ethernet header compression configuration IE).

results.question: Under what condition does the AMF include the Rejected NSSAI IE in a DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message during a network-initiated de-registration procedure?
results.reference: If the network de-registration is triggered due to network slice-specific authentication and authorization failure or revocation as specified in subclause 4.6.2.4, and the UE does not support extended rejected NSSAI, then the AMF shall include the Rejected NSSAI IE in the DEREGISTRATION REQUEST message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.3.1, Network-initiated de-registration procedure initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.19.16, Rejected NSSAI
results.model_answer: The AMF includes the Rejected NSSAI IE when it initiates de-registration with re-registration required because one or more S-NSSAIs previously allowed for the UE are no longer allowed/rejected.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.3.3 (network-initiated de-registration procedure; DEREGISTRATION REQUEST with re-registration required and Rejected NSSAI).

results.question: What triggers the UE to initiate the authentication and key agreement procedure for a 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay, and what is the first action the UE must take as part of that initiation?
results.reference: The procedure is triggered when the UE receives a ProSe direct link establishment request from a 5G ProSe remote UE including the SUCI of the remote UE, for establishing a secure PC5 unicast link. The first action the UE must take is to allocate an available PRTI value for the procedure and associate it with the 5G ProSe remote UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.4.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.4.2, ProSe relay transaction identity (PRTI)
results.model_answer: The UE initiates it when it intends to register to provide 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay service. Its first action is to send a REGISTRATION REQUEST with the 5GS registration type set to “5G ProSe UE-to-network relay registration.”
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1 (registration procedure) and the 5GS registration type IE definition in clause 9.11.3.7; see also the 5G ProSe UE-to-network relay procedures clause (release-dependent numbering).

results.question: For which PDU session types can IP header compression and Ethernet header compression be used, and what is a common procedural requirement for negotiating their configuration?
results.reference: The UE and the SMF may use IP header compression for PDU sessions of "IPv4", "IPv6", or "IPv4v6" PDU session type, and Ethernet header compression for PDU sessions of "Ethernet" PDU session type (Clause_6_2_16). A common requirement is that the header compression configuration for each PDU session is negotiated during the PDU session establishment procedure and PDU session modification procedure if both the UE and the network support header compression (Clause_6_2_16).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 6.2.16, Handling of header compression for control plane CIoT optimizations; TS 24.301, Clause 6.2.16, Handling of header compression for control plane CIoT optimizations
results.model_answer: IP header compression can be used for IPv4, IPv6, and IPv4v6 PDU sessions. Ethernet header compression can be used for Ethernet PDU sessions. Their use/configuration is negotiated between the UE and network using Protocol Configuration Options (PCO), typically during PDU session establishment or PDU session modification.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.10 (PDU session management), especially the PDU session establishment/modification procedures in clauses 5.10.2 and 5.10.3; see also the PCO handling specified for header-compression configuration.

results.question: Under what condition is the UE required to include the SM PDU DN request container IE in a PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message?
results.reference: This IE is included when the UE requests to establish a new PDU session with a DN and needs to provide information for the PDU session authentication and authorization by the external DN.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.1.8, SM PDU DN request container; TS 24.301, Clause 6.4.1.2, UE-requested PDU session establishment procedure initiation
results.model_answer: The UE shall include the SM PDU DN request container IE when it has received that IE from the network in a network-requested PDU session establishment procedure (i.e., it returns the received DN request container in its PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.3.2.1 (PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT REQUEST message; conditional presence of the SM PDU DN request container IE); see also clause 6.4.1.3 (network-requested PDU session establishment procedure).

results.question: What actions should a UE take if a service request for initiating an emergency PDU session is not accepted by the network and the UE remains in the same PLMN?
results.reference: As per Clause_5_6_1_6, if the service request for initiating an emergency PDU session cannot be accepted by the network and the UE is in the same selected PLMN where the last service request was attempted, the UE shall either a) inform the upper layers of the failure of the procedure, or b) de-register locally (if not already) and attempt initial registration for emergency services. This aligns with the UE's capability in the 5GMM-REGISTERED.LIMITED-SERVICE substate (Clause_5_2_3_2_4), where it may perform de-registration locally and initiate an initial registration for emergency services.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.1.6, Service request procedure for initiating an emergency PDU session not accepted by the network; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.3.2.4, LIMITED-SERVICE
results.model_answer: The UE shall initiate an emergency registration procedure in the same PLMN (i.e., perform registration with registration type set to "emergency registration").
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.6.1.4 (service request procedure rejected by the network): if a service request for initiating an emergency PDU session is not accepted and the UE remains in the same PLMN, the UE initiates the registration procedure for emergency services.

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE include the Service-level-AA container IE in a message, and which specific messages require it?
results.reference: The UE shall include the Service-level-AA container IE if the UE supporting UAS services requests a registration for UAS services (Clause_8_2_6_35). Furthermore, this IE shall be included in the message when the UE needs to establish a PDU session for the UAS services (Clause_8_3_1_16).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.35, Service-level-AA container; TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.1.16, Service-level-AA container
results.model_answer: A UE shall include the Service-level-AA container IE when it has a Service-level Authentication and Authorization (AA) container to provide to the network as part of NAS registration/service-request handling. It is included in the REGISTRATION REQUEST when initiating registration, or in the SERVICE REQUEST when initiating a service request; it is not included unconditionally when no such container is available/required.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, service-level-AA-container conditional-presence rules in the REGISTRATION REQUEST and SERVICE REQUEST procedures/message formats (see clauses 5.3.2.2 and 5.3.2.5, and the corresponding message IE tables in clause 8.2).

results.question: Under what conditions does a MUSIM UE include the 'Paging restriction' IE, and what is the purpose of the 'UE request type' IE in this context?
results.reference: The UE shall include the 'Paging restriction' IE if the Request type is set to 'NAS signalling connection release' or to 'Rejection of paging' in the UE request type IE and the UE requests the network to restrict paging. The 'UE request type' IE is included if the MUSIM UE requests the release of the NAS signalling connection or rejects the paging request from the network.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.16.7, Paging restriction; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.16.6, UE request type
results.model_answer: A MUSIM UE includes the Paging restriction IE in a SERVICE REQUEST when, due to activity/priority on another subscription, it requests the 5GS to restrict paging for that subscription. The UE request type IE identifies the nature of the service request (e.g. initial request versus request for an existing PDU session, including emergency variants), so the AMF can process the request and associated paging restriction appropriately.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.6.1.2.2 (Service Request procedure initiation / SERVICE REQUEST contents for MUSIM paging restriction); see also the UE request type and Paging restriction IE definitions in clause 9.11.3.

results.question: When is the network prohibited from including the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE in a message to the UE?
results.reference: According to Clause_8_2_7_39, the network shall include the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE only if several conditions are met. Two key prohibitive conditions are: 1) the UE is not performing the initial registration for emergency services, and 2) the UE does not have an active emergency PDU session. This is consistent with the UE behavior described in Clause_5_3_24, which states the UE shall not include its UE paging probability information (related to WUS) during a registration procedure when the UE has an active emergency PDU session.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.39, Negotiated WUS assistance information; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.24, WUS assistance
results.model_answer: The network shall not include the Negotiated WUS assistance information IE unless the UE has indicated support for WUS assistance information in the 5GMM capability IE (i.e., the WUS-assistance-information capability bit is set).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.8 (WUS assistance information procedure), in conjunction with clause 9.11.3 (5GMM capability IE / WUS assistance information capability).

results.question: According to the error handling procedures, what should the UE do if it receives a message with an unknown or unforeseen message type, and what is the purpose of the 5GMM status procedure?
results.reference: If UE receives a 5GMM message or 5GSM message with message type not defined for the extended protocol discriminator (EPD) or not implemented by the receiver, it shall return a status message (5GMM STATUS or 5GSM STATUS depending on the EPD) with cause #97 'message type non-existent or not implemented'. The purpose of the 5GMM status procedure is to report at any time in the 5GMM STATUS message certain error conditions detected upon receipt of 5GMM protocol data in the AMF or in the UE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.4, Unknown or unforeseen message type; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.6.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE shall send a 5GMM STATUS message. It uses 5GMM cause #97 ("message type non-existent or not implemented") for an unknown/unimplemented message type; if the message type is known but not expected in the current protocol state, cause #98 ("message type not compatible with the protocol state") applies. The 5GMM status procedure is used by the UE or network to report certain error conditions.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.5 (5GMM status procedure); see also the 5GMM error-handling rules and 5GMM cause values #97 and #98 in clause 9.11.3.1.

results.question: What should the UE do upon diagnosing a 'missing conditional IE' error in a received message, and what is the specified action for the UE when it receives a 5GSM STATUS message with cause value #97?
results.reference: When upon receipt of a 5GMM or 5GSM message the UE diagnoses a 'missing conditional IE' error, the UE shall ignore the message and shall return a status message (5GMM STATUS or 5GSM STATUS depending on the EPD) with cause #100 'conditional IE error'. If the 5GSM entity of the UE receives a 5GSM STATUS message with cause value #97 'Message type non-existent or not implemented', the UE shall abort any ongoing 5GSM procedure related to the PTI or PDU session ID and stop any related timer.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 7.7.2, Conditional IE errors; TS 24.301, Clause 6.5.2, 5GSM status received in the UE
results.model_answer: The UE shall discard the erroneous message and send the appropriate STATUS message with cause #100 "conditional IE error" (5GMM STATUS or 5GSM STATUS, as applicable). If the UE receives a 5GSM STATUS message with cause #97 "message type non-existent or not implemented", it shall take no further action.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.4.4 (handling of erroneous protocol data, including missing conditional IEs) and clause 6.4.4 (5GSM STATUS message handling).

results.question: Under what conditions is the UE allowed to initiate an initial registration for emergency services while in the 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION substate?
results.reference: According to Clause_5_2_2_3_3, the UE in 3GPP access may initiate an initial registration procedure for emergency services even if timers T3502, T3511 or T3346 are running. This is further supported by Clause_5_2_2_3_1, which states the UE may initiate an initial registration procedure for emergency services even if timer T3346 is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.3.3, ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.3.1, NORMAL-SERVICE
results.model_answer: The UE may initiate an initial registration for emergency services in 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION when emergency services are required, even though another registration procedure is ongoing. The emergency registration may pre-empt/replace the ongoing non-emergency registration attempt; this exception does not permit ordinary new registration attempts.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.3.1.2 (Registration procedure initiation), provisions for initiating registration for emergency services while in 5GMM-DEREGISTERED.ATTEMPTING-REGISTRATION; see also clause 5.1.3.2 (5GMM-DEREGISTERED state/substates).

results.question: Describe the interaction between the UE and network regarding ciphered broadcast assistance data, specifying the IEs involved from each side.
results.reference: For ciphered broadcast assistance data, the UE indicates its need for new ciphering keys by including the 'Additional information requested' IE. If the network then needs to provide that key data, it responds by including the 'Ciphering key data' IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.29, Additional information requested; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.35, Ciphering key data
results.model_answer: The UE requests the information by including the Ciphered Broadcast Assistance Data Request IE in the REGISTRATION REQUEST. If available/authorized, the network provides the corresponding Ciphered Broadcast Assistance Data IE in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT (and may update it using a CONFIGURATION UPDATE COMMAND).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 5.5.1.2.2 (REGISTRATION REQUEST handling), clause 5.5.1.2.4 (REGISTRATION ACCEPT handling), and the IE definitions in clause 9.11.

results.question: When is the Serving PLMN rate control IE included by the network, and to which type of PDU sessions is this control applicable?
results.reference: The Serving PLMN rate control IE shall be included when the network needs to indicate the maximum uplink control plane user data the UE is allowed to send per 6 minute interval (Clause_8_3_2_14). Serving PLMN rate control is applicable only for PDU sessions established for control plane CIoT 5GS optimization (Clause_6_2_14).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.3.2.14, Serving PLMN rate control; TS 24.301, Clause 6.2.14, Handling of Serving PLMN rate control
results.model_answer: The network includes the Serving PLMN rate control IE in the PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT when the established PDU session is subject to Serving PLMN rate control. The control is applicable to IP PDU sessions (IPv4, IPv6 or IPv4v6) and Ethernet PDU sessions, not unstructured PDU sessions.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 6.4.1.3 (PDU SESSION ESTABLISHMENT ACCEPT), Serving PLMN rate control IE inclusion; see also the Serving PLMN rate control IE definition in clause 9.11.4.

results.question: Under what condition would a UE include the 'Additional information requested' IE, and what action does the network take in response if that condition is met?
results.reference: The UE includes the 'Additional information requested' IE if it supports ciphered broadcast assistance data and needs to obtain new ciphering keys for it. In response, if the network needs to send ciphering key data to the UE for ciphered broadcast assistance data, it includes the 'Ciphering key data' IE.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.29, Additional information requested; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.35, Ciphering key data
results.model_answer: A UE includes the Additional information requested IE in a REGISTRATION REQUEST when it requests NSSRG (network slice-specific registration group) information from the network. On receiving this request, the network provides the NSSRG information to the UE, typically in the REGISTRATION ACCEPT message (when applicable).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clauses 5.5.1.2.2 and 5.5.1.3.2; IE definition in clause 9.11.3.1 (Additional information requested).

results.question: What triggers the network to include the 'Ciphering key data' IE, and what prior indication from the UE would typically lead to this situation?
results.reference: The network includes the 'Ciphering key data' IE if it needs to send ciphering key data to the UE for ciphered broadcast assistance data. This situation would typically be preceded by the UE including the 'Additional information requested' IE, which it does when it supports ciphered broadcast assistance data and needs new ciphering keys.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.7.35, Ciphering key data; TS 24.301, Clause 8.2.6.29, Additional information requested
results.model_answer: The network includes the Ciphering key data IE in a SECURITY MODE COMMAND when it establishes/updates an EPS NAS security context for S1-mode operation (i.e., it includes EPS NAS security algorithms). This would normally follow the UE indicating S1-mode capability in its 5GMM capability information.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 24.501, clause 8.2.26 (SECURITY MODE COMMAND, conditional IEs including EPS NAS security algorithms and Ciphering key data); see also clause 5.4.2.2 (NAS security mode control procedure and S1-mode/EPS security-context handling).

results.question: What are the two primary purposes of the DL Information Transfer procedure, and what message does the network send to initiate it?
results.reference: The two primary purposes of the DL Information Transfer procedure are to transfer NAS dedicated information from NG-RAN to a UE in RRC_CONNECTED or RRC_INACTIVE during SDT, and to transfer F1-C related information from IAB Donor-CU to IAB-DU via IAB-MT in RRC_CONNECTED. The network initiates the procedure by sending the DLInformationTransfer message.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.7.1.1, General DLInformationTransfer; TS 24.301, Clause 5.7.1.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The DL Information Transfer procedure is used to transfer (1) NAS dedicated information and (2) non-NAS dedicated information from the network to the UE. The network initiates it by sending a DLInformationTransfer message.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.2 (DL Information Transfer): purpose and initiation of the procedure; see also the DLInformationTransfer message definition in clause 6.2.2.

results.question: If a UE has a DAPS bearer configured and receives N310 consecutive 'out-of-sync' indications for the source SpCell while T304 is running, what action does it take regarding timer T310, and what subsequent action stops this timer?
results.reference: The UE shall start timer T310 for the source SpCell. Timer T310 for the corresponding SpCell is stopped upon receiving N311 consecutive 'in-sync' indications for the SpCell from lower layers while T310 is running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.10.1, Detection of physical layer problems in RRC_CONNECTED; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.10.2, Recovery of physical layer problems
results.model_answer: The UE starts T310 for the source SpCell. It subsequently stops T310 upon receiving N311 consecutive in-sync indications for the source SpCell from lower layers.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.10 (Radio link failure related procedures), specifically the DAPS/source-SpCell handling for N310 out-of-sync while T304 is running and the N311 in-sync condition for stopping T310.

results.question: During SpCell configuration, if the SpCellConfig contains rlf-TimersAndConstants, how does the UE configure the RLF timers and constants? Furthermore, if the received rlf-TimersAndConstants is set to 'release' and a DAPS bearer is configured, what values are used for timers T301, T310, T311 and constants N310, N311?
results.reference: The UE configures the RLF timers and constants for this cell group as specified in 5.3.5.5.6. If rlf-TimersAndConstants is set to 'release' and a DAPS bearer is configured, the UE uses values for timers T301, T310, T311 and constants N310, N311 for the target cell group, as included in ue-TimersAndConstants received in SIB1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.5.7, SpCell Configuration; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.5.6, RLF Timers & Constants configuration
results.model_answer: If SpCellConfig includes rlf-TimersAndConstants with a configured value, the UE configures RLF timers T301, T310 and T311 and constants N310 and N311 according to that IE. If rlf-TimersAndConstants is set to release and a DAPS bearer is configured, the UE uses the values of T301, T310, T311, N310 and N311 configured in the previous cell group.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.4, Actions related to reception of an RRCReconfiguration (SpCellConfig/rlf-TimersAndConstants handling).

results.question: What must a UE do when it receives a command to remove a sidelink measurement object (sl-MeasObjectId), and what is the purpose of the MeasurementReportSidelink procedure?
results.reference: For each sl-MeasObjectId included in the received sl-MeasObjectToRemoveList that is part of the current configuration, the UE must remove the corresponding entry from the sl-MeasObjectList, remove all associated sl-MeasIds from the sl-MeasIdList, and for each removed sl-MeasId, remove its reporting entry from VarMeasReportListSL and stop its periodical reporting timer. The purpose of the MeasurementReportSidelink procedure is to transfer measurement results from the UE to the peer UE associated.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.10.2.4, Sidelink measurement object removal; TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.10.5.1, General MeasurementReportSidelink
results.model_answer: For each sl-MeasObjectId in sl-MeasObjectToRemoveList, the UE shall remove the corresponding sidelink measurement object. The MeasurementReportSidelink procedure enables the UE to report configured sidelink measurement results to the network.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.2 (sidelink measurement configuration processing; sl-MeasObjectToRemoveList) and clause 5.5.5 (MeasurementReportSidelink procedure purpose).

results.question: Under what conditions does the handover to NR procedure apply when transferring a connection from another RAT, and what is the network's responsibility regarding ciphering during this process?
results.reference: The handover to NR procedure applies when SRBs, possibly in combination with DRBs, are established in another RAT. During this procedure, the network applies it to activate ciphering, possibly using NULL algorithm, if not yet activated in the other RAT.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.1, General RRCReconfiguration (sent via other RAT) RRCReconfigurationComplete; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: The handover to NR procedure applies when a UE in RRC_CONNECTED is transferred from E-UTRA or another RAT to NR. The network shall ensure that ciphering is activated before initiating the handover-to-NR procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.2 (Handover to NR).

results.question: What procedure is used by an IAB-MT to request IP addresses from the IAB-donor-CU, and what specific message field is set when IPv4 addresses are requested?
results.reference: The IAB Other Information procedure is used by IAB-MT to request the IAB-donor-CU to allocate IP addresses. When IPv4 addresses are requested, the IAB-MT sets the iab-IPv4-AddressNumReq to the number of IPv4 addresses requested per specific usage.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.7.12.1, General IAB-MT Network IABOtherInformation; TS 24.301, Clause 5.7.12.3, Actions related to transmission of IABOtherInformation message
results.model_answer: The IAB-MT uses the IAB-IP-AddressRequest procedure/message to request IP address allocation from the IAB-donor-CU. For an IPv4 request, it sets requestedIP-AddressType-r16 to ipv4.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.10.2 (IAB-IP-AddressRequest procedure; most likely reference), and the IAB-IP-AddressRequest-r16-IEs ASN.1 definition for requestedIP-AddressType-r16 (ipv4, ipv6, ipv4v6).

results.question: What triggers the initiation of the SCGFailureInformation procedure, and what is one specific action the UE takes upon initiating it?
results.reference: The procedure is initiated upon detecting radio link failure for the SCG, in accordance with clause 5.3.10.3 (as per Clause_5_7_3_2). Upon initiating the procedure, if it was not initiated due to beam failure of the PSCell while the SCG is deactivated, the UE shall suspend SCG transmission for all SRBs, DRBs and, if any, BH RLC channels (as per Clause_5_7_3_2).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.7.3.2, Initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.10.3, Detection of radio link failure
results.model_answer: The UE initiates the SCGFailureInformation procedure upon detecting an SCG failure. Upon initiation, one specific UE action is to suspend transmission on the SCG (for example, suspend SCG radio bearers).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3.2 (SCGFailureInformation procedure — Initiation): the UE shall initiate the procedure when it detects SCG failure and perform specified SCG suspension actions.

results.question: What are two types of information that a UE can report to the network using the SidelinkUEInformationNR procedure, specifically related to interactions with a peer UE?
results.reference: The UE can report the sidelink UE capability information of the associated peer UE for unicast communication (Clause_5_8_3_1). It can also report the RLC mode information of the sidelink data radio bearer(s) received from the associated peer UE for unicast communication (Clause_5_8_3_1).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.3.1, General SIB12 acquisition SidelinkUEInformationNR; TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.3.1, General SIB12 acquisition SidelinkUEInformationNR
results.model_answer: A UE can report (1) sidelink transmission resource requirements for data it intends to transmit to a peer UE, and (2) sidelink reception-interest information, i.e., the NR frequencies on which it is interested in receiving sidelink transmissions from a peer UE.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3 (Sidelink UE information), especially 5.7.3.2 (Initiation); see also the commTxResourceReq and commRxInterestedFreqList fields in SidelinkUEInformationNR-IEs.

results.question: If the SpCellConfig contains spCellConfigDedicated and any of the reference signals used for radio link monitoring are reconfigured by it, what actions does the UE take regarding timers T310, T312 and counters N310, N311? What is one condition under which timer T310 for a cell group would also be stopped according to RLF timer configuration procedures?
results.reference: The UE shall stop timer T310 for the corresponding SpCell (if running), stop timer T312 for the corresponding SpCell (if running), and reset the counters N310 and N311. According to RLF timer configuration, if the received rlf-TimersAndConstants is not set to 'release' and a DAPS bearer is configured, the UE shall stop timer T310 for this cell group, if running.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.5.7, SpCell Configuration; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.5.6, RLF Timers & Constants configuration
results.model_answer: The UE stops T310 and T312 for the concerned cell group and resets N310 and N311. One RLF-procedure condition for stopping T310 is receipt of N311 consecutive in-sync indications from lower layers while T310 is running for that cell group.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5 (RRCReconfiguration/SpCellConfig handling) and clause 5.3.10.1 (radio link failure detection: stop T310 upon N311 consecutive in-sync indications).

results.question: What actions does the UE perform upon receiving an RRCReject message?
results.reference: The UE shall perform the actions as specified in 5.3.15.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.3.5, Reception of the RRCReject by the UE; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.13.10, Reception of the RRCReject by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE stops T300. If RRCReject includes waitTime and/or extendedWaitTime, it starts T302 with the indicated value (the extendedWaitTime value applies when present). The UE then performs cell selection in accordance with TS 38.304.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.4, "Actions upon reception of RRCReject by the UE".

results.question: What actions must the UE take if gapSharingFR1 is set to setup and an FR1 measurement gap sharing configuration is already configured?
results.reference: The UE shall release the existing FR1 measurement gap sharing configuration configured by gapSharingFR1 and then setup the new FR1 measurement gap sharing configuration indicated by the measGapSharingConfig in accordance with the received gapSharingFR1.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.11, Measurement gap sharing configuration
results.model_answer: The UE shall release the already configured FR1 measurement gap sharing configuration, and then configure the FR1 measurement gap sharing configuration according to gapSharingFR1.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Measurement configuration), UE actions for gapSharingFR1 set to setup.

results.question: What actions does the UE perform when a CellGroupConfig IE contains the rlc-BearerToReleaseList, and what specific procedure is triggered for each logical channel identity in that list?
results.reference: When the CellGroupConfig contains the rlc-BearerToReleaseList, the UE performs RLC bearer release as specified in 5.3.5.5.3. For each logicalChannelIdentity value included in the rlc-BearerToReleaseList that is part of the current UE configuration within the same cell group, the UE releases the RLC entity or entities as specified in TS 38.322, clause 5.1.3, and releases the corresponding logical channel.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.5.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.5.3, RLC bearer release
results.model_answer: For each logicalChannelIdentity in rlc-BearerToReleaseList, the UE releases the corresponding RLC bearer (including its associated logical-channel configuration) and performs the RLC entity release procedure for that RLC entity.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (RLC bearer configuration; processing of rlc-BearerToReleaseList).

results.question: What is the common first step the UE must take when setting up a new measurement gap configuration for FR1, whether it's a standard gap or a gap sharing configuration, if one is already configured?
results.reference: In both cases, if a configuration is already setup, the UE must first release the existing FR1 measurement gap configuration (for standard gaps) or the existing FR1 measurement gap sharing configuration (for gap sharing) before setting up the new one.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.9, Measurement gap configuration; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.11, Measurement gap sharing configuration
results.model_answer: The UE must first release the already configured measurement gap configuration for FR1 before configuring the new standard FR1 gap or FR1 gap-sharing configuration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Measurement configuration), UE actions for measGapConfig: for both gapFR1 setup and gapSharingFR1 setup, if a measurement gap configuration for FR1 is already configured, the UE releases it before applying the new configuration.

results.question: What must the UE do if gapFR1 is set to setup and an FR1 measurement gap configuration is already configured?
results.reference: The UE shall release the existing FR1 measurement gap configuration and then setup the new FR1 measurement gap configuration indicated by gapFR1 in accordance with the received gapOffset, applying the specified timing advance mgta and associating the gap with the measGapId if present.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.9, Measurement gap configuration
results.model_answer: The UE shall reconfigure the existing FR1 measurement gap configuration in accordance with gapFR1.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2.6 (Measurement gap configuration): behaviour specified for gapFR1 set to setup when an FR1 measurement gap configuration is already configured.

results.question: During a Secondary Cell Group (SCG) release, what procedure is performed for each RLC bearer that is part of the SCG configuration, and what does that procedure entail?
results.reference: During an SCG release, for each RLC bearer that is part of the SCG configuration, the UE performs the RLC bearer release procedure as specified in 5.3.5.5.3. This procedure entails releasing the RLC entity or entities as specified in TS 38.322, clause 5.1.3, and releasing the corresponding logical channel.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.4, Secondary cell group release; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.5.3, RLC bearer release
results.model_answer: For each RLC bearer that is part of the released SCG configuration, the UE performs RLC re-establishment. This re-establishes the associated RLC entity: its RLC state and timers are reset and buffered RLC data (including transmission/retransmission data, as applicable) is discarded, in accordance with the RLC mode-specific re-establishment rules.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3 (actions upon RRCReconfiguration/SCG release) requires RLC re-establishment for each RLC bearer in the SCG configuration. The re-establishment actions are specified in 3GPP TS 38.322, clause 5.2 (RLC re-establishment).

results.question: From which RAT is the RRCReconfiguration message sent to initiate a handover to NR, and what is a prerequisite for handover specifically from E-UTRA?
results.reference: The RRCReconfiguration message is sent via the radio access technology from which the inter-RAT handover is performed. A prerequisite for handover from E-UTRA to NR is that integrity has been activated in E-UTRA.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.2, Initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.1, General RRCReconfiguration (sent via other RAT) RRCReconfigurationComplete
results.model_answer: For handover from E-UTRA to NR, the NR RRCReconfiguration is conveyed by the E-UTRA source RAT, embedded in an E-UTRA RRCConnectionReconfiguration message. A prerequisite is that the UE is in RRC_CONNECTED in E-UTRA.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Handover; in particular the E-UTRA-to-NR handover initiation text). See also TS 36.331 RRCConnectionReconfiguration support for carrying the NR RRCReconfiguration.

results.question: What actions does the UE perform upon receiving an RRCRelease message?
results.reference: The UE shall perform the actions as specified in 5.3.8.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.13.9, Reception of the RRCRelease by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE stops the relevant RRC supervision timers and, depending on the presence of suspendConfig, either: (1) performs RRC suspension, stores the required AS context/configuration and enters RRC_INACTIVE; or (2) releases the RRC-established radio resources/AS bearers and enters RRC_IDLE. In RRC_IDLE, it applies any included redirection, cell-reselection-priority, deprioritisation or idle-mode mobility-control information for subsequent cell selection/reselection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.8.3, "Reception of an RRCRelease by the UE" (with RRC suspension details in the associated RRCRelease suspension procedure).

results.question: Under what RRC state(s) can a UE initiate the UL Information Transfer procedure for NAS information, and what additional condition must be met for an IAB-MT to initiate it for F1-C information?
results.reference: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED or a UE in RRC_INACTIVE during SDT can initiate the UL Information Transfer procedure for NAS dedicated information. For an IAB-MT in RRC_CONNECTED to initiate the procedure for F1-C related information, SBR2 or split SRB2 must be established.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.7.2.1, General ULInformationTransfer; TS 24.301, Clause 5.7.2.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: A UE may initiate UL Information Transfer for NAS information in RRC_CONNECTED or RRC_INACTIVE. An IAB-MT may initiate it for F1-C information only in RRC_CONNECTED and only if it is not configured with a BH RLC channel for F1-C.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.1 (UL Information Transfer—procedure initiation).

results.question: What common principle applies when a UE cannot include all requested information (band combinations or feature sets) in a capability response message, whether for sidelink or general MRDC capabilities?
results.reference: In both cases, if the UE cannot include all requested items due to message size or list size constraints, it is up to the UE implementation to decide which items to prioritize for inclusion.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.9.2.4, Actions related to reception of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE; TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.1.4, Setting band combinations, feature set combinations and feature sets supported by the UE
results.model_answer: The UE reports a supported, internally consistent subset of the requested information when it cannot fit all requested band combinations or feature sets in the capability response. The subset selection/prioritisation is UE-implementation dependent; the UE is not required to report every requested item.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.6.1.3 (UE capability information): capability-reporting rules for requested sidelink band combinations and NR MRDC band combinations/feature sets allow reporting a subset when all requested information cannot be included.

results.question: What is the purpose of the handover procedure initiated by a RAN using another RAT, and what specific actions does the network perform on the SRBs and DRBs?
results.reference: The purpose of the procedure is to transfer a connection between the UE and another Radio Access Network (e.g. E-UTRAN) to NR under network control. The network applies the procedure to re-establish SRBs and one or more DRBs.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.1, General RRCReconfiguration (sent via other RAT) RRCReconfigurationComplete; TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: Its purpose is to transfer the UE’s RRC connection from the source cell/RAN to a target cell/RAN of another RAT while preserving service continuity. The network provides the target-side radio-bearer configuration: it adds/modifies SRBs (and may release SRB3) and adds/modifies and/or releases DRBs as required for the handover.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Handover), especially 5.5.2.1 (General); radio-bearer actions are specified by RadioBearerConfig in clause 6.3.2 (RRCReconfiguration IEs: srb-ToAddModList, srb3-ToRelease, drb-ToAddModList, drb-ToReleaseList).

results.question: What is the purpose of the UEAssistanceInformationSidelink procedure, and under what condition may a UE initiate sending this message to its peer?
results.reference: The purpose of the UEAssistanceInformationSidelink procedure is for a UE to inform its peer UE of the sidelink DRX assistance information used to determine the sidelink DRX configuration for unicast communication (Clause_5_8_9_6_1). A UE may initiate sending this message when the sidelink DRX assistance information has not been sent previously or when the previously transmitted sidelink DRX assistance information has changed (Clause_5_8_9_6_2).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.9.6.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.9.6.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: It lets a UE provide sidelink assistance information (e.g., its sidelink DRX preference) to a peer UE. A UE may initiate it when it has assistance information to provide to that peer UE over the PC5-RRC connection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause titled "UEAssistanceInformationSidelink" (sidelink RRC procedures; purpose and initiation conditions).

results.question: What actions does the UE perform upon receiving SIB6?
results.reference: Upon receiving the SIB6, the UE shall perform the actions as specified in 5.2.2.4.7.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.7, Actions upon reception of SIB6
results.model_answer: Upon receiving SIB6, the UE forwards the ETWS primary-notification information to upper layers, including the message identifier, serial number, warning type, and warning security information (if present).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2.5 (ETWS primary notification / reception of SIB6); SIB6 definition in clause 6.3.1.

results.question: What actions must a UE take upon receiving SIB12 if it is configured to receive NR sidelink communication and sl-FreqInfoList is included in sl-ConfigCommonNR?
results.reference: Upon receiving SIB12, if sl-FreqInfoList is included in sl-ConfigCommonNR and the UE is configured to receive NR sidelink communication, it must use the resource pool(s) indicated by sl-RxPool for NR sidelink communication reception, as specified in 5.8.7.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.13, Actions upon reception of SIB12; TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.7, Sidelink communication reception
results.model_answer: The UE shall use the common NR sidelink configuration in SIB12 for sidelink reception and, for each frequency represented in sl-FreqInfoList, consider/configure that frequency for NR sidelink communication reception (using the corresponding SL frequency information/configuration).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.1 (sidelink communication/reception procedure; the “Upon receiving SIB12” requirements for a UE configured to receive NR sidelink communication), in particular the conditional processing of sl-FreqInfoList in sl-ConfigCommonNR.

results.question: How does a UE determine the MBS frequencies of interest, and what is the relationship between this determination and the contents of the MBS Interest Indication?
results.reference: The UE determines the MBS frequencies of interest by considering a frequency to be part of the set if: 1) at least one MBS session the UE is receiving or interested to receive via a broadcast MRB is ongoing or about to start; 2) for at least one of these sessions, SIB21 from the PCell includes for the concerned frequency one or more MBS FSAIs as indicated in the USD for this session; and 3) the UE's supportedBandCombination contains at least one band combination including the set of MBS frequencies of interest. When setting the contents of the MBS Interest Indication, if the set of MBS frequencies of interest (determined per 5.9.4.3) is not empty, the UE must include mbs-FreqList and set it to include these MBS frequencies of interest sorted by decreasing order of interest.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.9.4.3, MBS frequencies of interest determination; TS 24.301, Clause 5.9.4.5, Setting of the contents of MBS Interest Indication
results.model_answer: The UE determines its MBS frequencies of interest from the MBS service information/interest provided by upper layers (i.e. the frequencies on which the MBS services that the UE wants to receive are available). When it performs the MBS Interest Indication procedure, the UE reports those determined frequencies in the `mbs-FreqList` of `MBSInterestIndication`, subject to the field’s presence/conditional-inclusion rules. Thus, the frequency list in the indication conveys the UE’s MBS frequencies of interest to the network; it is not an independently selected network frequency list.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.1 (MBS interest indication procedure), especially the UE actions for constructing `MBSInterestIndication` and populating `mbs-FreqList`; see also the `MBSInterestIndication` / `MBSInterestIndication-r17-IEs` ASN.1 and field description in clause 6.2.2.

results.question: When a peer UE receives a UECapabilityEnquirySidelink message, how does it compile and prioritize the list of candidate band combinations for inclusion in the UECapabilityInformationSidelink message?
results.reference: The peer UE compiles a list of 'candidate band combinations' consisting only of bands included in the received frequencyBandListFilterSidelink. It prioritizes them in the order they appear in the frequencyBandListFilterSidelink (i.e., first including combinations with the first-listed band, then the second, and so on).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.9.2.4, Actions related to reception of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE; TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.9.2.3, Actions related to transmission of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE
results.model_answer: The peer UE forms the candidate list by intersecting the band combinations requested in sl-RequestedUECapabilityBandCombinationList with its own supported sidelink band combinations. It includes only combinations that it supports, and orders the reported candidates according to the order/priority of the requested list (earlier requested combinations have higher priority). The resulting sidelink capability information is carried in UECapabilityInformationSidelink.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause covering the sidelink UE-capability-transfer procedure (receipt of UECapabilityEnquirySidelink and transmission of UECapabilityInformationSidelink); see also the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink and UECapabilityInformationSidelink IE definitions in clause 6.3.

results.question: According to the clauses, which SIBs share the same general principle regarding UE requirements for their contents as the MBSBroadcastConfiguration message?
results.reference: SIB3, SIB5, SIB20, and SIB21 share the same general principle as the MBSBroadcastConfiguration message. For all of them, no UE requirements related to their contents apply other than those specified elsewhere, such as within procedures using the concerned system information and/or within the corresponding field descriptions.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.9.2.4, Actions upon reception of the MBSBroadcastConfiguration message; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.4, Actions upon reception of SIB3; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.6, Actions upon reception of SIB5; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.22, Actions upon reception of SIB20; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.23, Actions upon reception of SIB21
results.model_answer: All SIBs other than SIB1 share the principle: the UE acquires/uses their contents only when required for the UE's operation or supported services; it is not generally required to acquire every such SIB. MBSBroadcastConfiguration follows this same on-demand SI-acquisition principle.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.1 (System information), especially the general SI-acquisition rules and the MBSBroadcastConfiguration description; SIB1 is the exception because it is required for initial access/system-information scheduling.

results.question: When the network modifies a reportConfig for a measId, what actions must the UE take regarding the measurement reporting entry and timers, and what is the general rule for configuring measurement objects for the SpCell and SCells within a Cell Group (CG)?
results.reference: For each measId associated with the modified reportConfigId, the UE must remove the measurement reporting entry for this measId from the VarMeasReportList (if included) and stop the periodical reporting timer or timer T321 or timer T322 (whichever one is running) and reset the associated information (e.g., timeToTrigger). Furthermore, the network must ensure that whenever the UE has a measConfig associated with a CG, it includes a measObject for the SpCell and for each NR SCell of the CG to be measured.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.7, Reporting configuration addition/modification; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.2.1, General
results.model_answer: If a reportConfig associated with a measId is modified, the UE shall remove the measurement-reporting entry for that measId (if present) and stop any running TTT and periodic-reporting timer associated with that measId. Measurement objects are configured per Cell Group: the network configures objects for the SpCell and, where measurements are required, for SCells; objects are frequency/reference-signal based and can serve cells in that CG sharing the applicable measurement frequency/configuration.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.2 (Measurement configuration), in particular the UE actions when a reportConfig associated with a measId is modified and the CG-specific measurement-object configuration rules.

results.question: What is a key difference in the release procedure for a broadcast MRB compared to a multicast MRB regarding the handling of lower layer entities?
results.reference: Upon broadcast MRB release, the UE shall release the PDCP entity, RLC entity as well as the related MAC and physical layer configuration. For multicast MRB release, the UE releases the PDCP entity and the mrb-Identity, but whether or not the RLC and MAC entities associated with this PDCP entity are reset or released is determined by the CellGroupConfig.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.9.3.4, Broadcast MRB release; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.6.6, Multicast MRB release
results.model_answer: For a broadcast MRB release, the UE releases the associated lower-layer entities. For a multicast MRB release, the UE releases the MRB but retains the associated lower-layer entities (they may remain usable for other multicast MRBs).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.5 (radio bearer configuration processing in RRCReconfiguration), specifically the MRB-to-release processing distinguishing broadcast MRBs from multicast MRBs.

results.question: If timer T390 is running for an Access Category when the access barring check procedure is initiated, what is the immediate outcome for the access attempt? What is the outcome if timer T302 is running and the Access Category is '0'?
results.reference: If timer T390 is running for the Access Category, the UE shall consider the access attempt as barred. If timer T302 is running and the Access Category is '0', the UE shall consider the access attempt as allowed.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.14.2, Initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.14.5, Access barring check
results.model_answer: If T390 is running for the applicable Access Category, the UE shall abort the access attempt. If T302 is running and the Access Category is '0', the UE shall also abort the access attempt.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.14 (Access barring check procedure): conditions for an Access Category '0' with T302 running and for T390 running require the UE to abort the access attempt.

results.question: In the context of sidelink UE capability transfer, what must the initiating UE include in the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink message, and what constraint does this have in common with the general UE capability transfer procedure for the E-UTRA network?
results.reference: The initiating UE must include the frequencyBandListFilterSidelink field, and it is not allowed to send the message without it. This is similar to the general UE capability transfer procedure where NOTE 1 states that a capability enquiry without a frequencyBandListFilter is not supported.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.9.2.3, Actions related to transmission of the UECapabilityEnquirySidelink by the UE; TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.1.4, Setting band combinations, feature set combinations and feature sets supported by the UE
results.model_answer: The initiating UE shall include ue-CapabilityRAT-RequestList in UECapabilityEnquirySidelink. As in the general UE capability-transfer procedure, the list shall not contain more than one UE-CapabilityRAT-Request for E-UTRA (rat-Type = eutra).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.6.4 (UE capability transfer for sidelink); see also clause 5.6.1 (General UE capability transfer requirements for E-UTRA).

results.question: Which clause provides a specific UE action that contrasts with the numerous clauses that state no general requirements apply to message contents?
results.reference: Clause 5.2.2.4.16 (Actions upon reception of SIBpos) provides a specific UE action. It states that upon receiving SIB15 (referenced within the clause text), the UE shall forward the applicable PLMNs with disaster condition for each PLMN sharing the cell to upper layers. This is a concrete requirement, unlike the other clauses which state that no general requirements apply beyond those specified elsewhere.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.16, Actions upon reception of SIBpos; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.4, Actions upon reception of SIB3
results.model_answer: Clause 5.3.3.3 provides a specific UE action: upon receiving an RRCSetup, the UE stops T300, enters RRC_CONNECTED and sends RRCSetupComplete, rather than merely having no general message-content requirements.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.3.3, "Reception of an RRCSetup by the UE".

results.question: When does a UE apply the MCCH information acquisition procedure, and how does it acquire the MCCH information upon entering a new cell?
results.reference: A UE applies the MCCH information acquisition procedure upon becoming interested to receive MBS broadcast services, upon entering a cell providing SIB20 (e.g., upon power on, following UE mobility), upon receiving a notification that the MCCH information has changed due to the start of new MBS service(s), or, if the UE is receiving data via broadcast MRB, upon receiving a notification that the MCCH information has changed due to MCCH information modification other than the change caused by the start of new MBS session(s). Specifically, when the UE enters a cell broadcasting SIB20, it shall acquire the MBSBroadcastConfiguration message on MCCH at the next repetition period.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.9.2.2, Initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 5.9.2.3, MCCH information acquisition by the UE
results.model_answer: A UE applies the MCCH information acquisition procedure when it enters a cell that provides MBS and the UE is interested in receiving an MBS service in that cell. Upon entering the new cell, the UE first obtains the MBS/MCCH configuration broadcast in SIB20 and then receives/decodes the MCCH at the MCCH occasions determined by that configuration, thereby acquiring the MCCH information (including the applicable MBS session information).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.8.1 (MCCH information acquisition); see also the SIB20 definition in clause 6.3.1 for the broadcast MBS/MCCH configuration.

results.question: In which RRC states does the SI acquisition procedure apply, and what is one of the main RRC functions related to broadcasting that supports this procedure?
results.reference: The SI acquisition procedure applies to UEs in RRC_IDLE, in RRC_INACTIVE, and in RRC_CONNECTED (Clause 5.2.2.1). One of the main RRC functions that supports this is the 'Broadcast of system information' (Clause 4.4).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.1, General UE requirements MIB SIB1 SystemInformationRequest SystemInformation messages; TS 24.301, Clause 4.4, Functions
results.model_answer: The SI acquisition procedure applies in RRC_IDLE and RRC_INACTIVE. A main supporting RRC function is the broadcast of system information related to AS and NAS.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.1 (SI acquisition in RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE) and clause 5.1 (RRC main functions, including broadcast of system information).

results.question: What is the procedure for releasing a BH RLC channel when it is triggered as a result of an SCG release, and which clause defines the SCG release trigger?
results.reference: For each BH-RLC-ChannelID value that is to be released as the result of an SCG release according to 5.3.5.4, the procedure is to release the RLC entity or entities as specified in TS 38.322, clause 5.1.3, and release the corresponding logical channel. The SCG release trigger is defined in clause 5.3.5.4.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.5.10, BH RLC channel release; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.4, Secondary cell group release
results.model_answer: When SCG release triggers BH RLC-channel release, the IAB-MT releases the BH RLC channel(s) associated with the released SCG, including the corresponding RLC entity and MAC logical channel. The SCG-release-triggered release is performed as part of the SCG release handling rather than as an independent BH RLC-channel release indication.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3.1 (SCG release trigger/handling); BH RLC-channel release requirements are in the RRCReconfiguration reception procedure of clause 5.3.5.3.

results.question: What actions does the UE take upon receiving a RadioBearerConfig IE that includes an mrb-ToReleaseList, and what specific steps are performed for each multicast MRB to be released?
results.reference: Upon receiving a RadioBearerConfig IE that includes an mrb-ToReleaseList, the UE shall perform multicast MRB release as specified in 5.3.5.6.6. For each mrb-Identity value included in the mrb-ToReleaseList that is part of the current UE configuration, the UE shall release the PDCP entity and the mrb-Identity, and indicate the release of the multicast MRB and the tmgi of the released multicast MRB to upper layers.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.6.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.6.6, Multicast MRB release
results.model_answer: If RadioBearerConfig contains mrb-ToReleaseList, the UE processes each listed mrb-Identity. For each multicast MRB, the UE releases the MRB, releases its associated PDCP entity if applicable, releases the associated RLC entity or entities, and releases the associated logical channel.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.3, "Reception of an RRCReconfiguration by the UE"—RadioBearerConfig processing for mrb-ToReleaseList.

results.question: How does the requirement statement for SIBpos differ from the requirement statements for SIB3, SIB5, SIB20, and SIB21?
results.reference: The requirement statement for SIBpos differs by specifying an external technical specification (TS 37.355) as a location for other applicable requirements, whereas the statements for SIB3, SIB5, SIB20, and SIB21 refer more generally to 'procedures using the concerned system information' and 'corresponding field descriptions'.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.16, Actions upon reception of SIBpos; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.4, Actions upon reception of SIB3; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.6, Actions upon reception of SIB5; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.22, Actions upon reception of SIB20; TS 24.301, Clause 5.2.2.4.23, Actions upon reception of SIB21
results.model_answer: SIBpos is demand/positioning-driven: the UE acquires it only when positioning SI is needed/requested. In contrast, SIB3, SIB5, SIB20 and SIB21 are acquired when their respective cell-selection/reselection or NTN applicability conditions require them; they are not conditioned on a positioning request.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.2.2 (System information acquisition), in particular the SI-acquisition requirements for SIB3/SIB5/SIB20/SIB21 versus SIBpos.

results.question: In which cases is an RRC connection establishment initiated for a UE configured to transmit NR sidelink communication?
results.reference: An RRC connection establishment is initiated for a UE configured to transmit NR sidelink communication if related data is available for transmission, and if the frequency on which the UE is configured to transmit NR sidelink communication is included in sl-FreqInfoList within SIB12 provided by the cell on which the UE camps, and if the valid version of SIB12 does not include sl-TxPoolSelectedNormal for the concerned frequency.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.3.1, General; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.13.1, General
results.model_answer: For an RRC_IDLE UE configured for NR sidelink transmission, RRC connection establishment is initiated when the UE needs to transmit sidelink data but has no applicable sidelink transmission configuration/resources (e.g. no suitable broadcast or preconfigured sidelink resource pool), or when it needs to send sidelink UE information to the network and is not already connected. In RRC_INACTIVE, the corresponding action is RRC resume rather than RRC connection establishment.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.1.1 (RRC connection establishment—General/initiating conditions); see also clause 5.8.3 (Sidelink UE information).

results.question: What are two scenarios in which a UE in RRC_CONNECTED, performing sidelink unicast with resource allocation mode 1, may report information received from its peer UE to the network?
results.reference: The UE may report the sidelink DRX assistance information received within the UEAssistanceInformationSidelink from its peer UE to the network (Clause_5_8_9_6_3). It may also report the sidelink DRX configuration received from the associated peer UE for NR sidelink unicast communication (Clause_5_8_3_1).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.9.6.3, Actions related to reception of UEAssistanceInformationSidelink message; TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.3.1, General SIB12 acquisition SidelinkUEInformationNR
results.model_answer: Two such cases are: (1) the UE receives sidelink DRX information/configuration from its unicast peer UE and reports the peer’s SL-DRX information to the gNB so that mode-1 scheduling can account for the peer UE’s DRX availability; and (2) the UE receives a sidelink CSI report from its peer UE and reports that sidelink CSI information to the gNB for mode-1 sidelink scheduling/link adaptation.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.1.4 (Sidelink UE information procedure), in particular the mode-1 sidelink-unicast reporting provisions for peer-received sl-DRX-Info and sl-CSI-Report.

results.question: What actions does the UE perform upon receiving an RRCReconfiguration message, and what specific procedure is executed if the message includes a reconfigurationWithSync?
results.reference: Upon reception of the RRCReconfiguration, the UE performs the RRC reconfiguration procedure as specified in 5.3.5. If the RRCReconfiguration includes a reconfigurationWithSync, the UE executes the reconfiguration with sync procedure as specified in 5.3.5.5.2.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.4.2.3, Reception of the RRCReconfiguration by the UE; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.5.2, Reconfiguration with sync
results.model_answer: Upon reception of RRCReconfiguration, the UE checks whether reconfigurationWithSync is included. If included, the UE performs the RRC reconfiguration with sync procedure; otherwise, it performs the normal RRC reconfiguration procedure.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.5.4 (Actions related to reception of RRCReconfiguration by the UE); reconfigurationWithSync case: clause 5.3.5.5 (RRC reconfiguration with sync).

results.question: What actions does a UE take if cell reselection occurs while T319 is running and the UE has a configured srs-PosRRC-InactiveConfig?
results.reference: The UE shall perform the actions upon going to RRC_IDLE as specified in 5.3.11 with release cause 'RRC Resume failure' (as per Clause_5_3_13_6). Additionally, the UE shall consider the Timing Advance value for SRS for Positioning transmission to be invalid and release the srs-PosRRC-InactiveConfig (as per Clause_5_7_15_2).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.13.6, Cell re-selection or cell selection or L2 U2N relay (re)selection while T390, T319, T319a or T302 is running (UE in RRC_INACTIVE); TS 24.301, Clause 5.7.15.2, Actions Related to SRS for Positioning at Cell Re-selection in RRC_INACTIVE
results.model_answer: The UE stops T319 and initiates a new RNA update procedure following the cell reselection.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.3.4.3 (Cell reselection in RRC_INACTIVE); see the condition for cell reselection while T319 is running with srs-PosRRC-InactiveConfig configured.

results.question: Under what conditions must a UE in RRC_CONNECTED initiate transmission of an MBS Interest Indication message, and what specific information must be included in that message when the set of MBS frequencies of interest is not empty?
results.reference: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED must initiate transmission of an MBS Interest Indication message if, upon initiating the procedure, SIB21 is provided by the PCell and the set of MBS frequencies of interest (determined per 5.9.4.3) is not empty and the UE did not transmit MBS Interest Indication since last entering RRC_CONNECTED or since the last transmission the UE connected to a PCell not broadcasting SIB21. Alternatively, it must transmit if the set of MBS frequencies of interest is different from the last transmission or if the prioritisation of reception of all indicated MBS broadcast frequencies compared to unicast reception has changed. When setting the contents and the set of MBS frequencies of interest is not empty, the UE must include mbs-FreqList set to include the MBS frequencies of interest sorted by decreasing order of interest, using absoluteFrequencySSB for serving frequency and ARFCN-ValueNR(s) from SIB21 for neighbouring frequencies. It must also include mbs-Priority if the UE prioritises reception of all indicated MBS frequencies above unicast/multicast reception, and if SIB20 is scheduled by the PCell, it must include mbs-ServiceList indicating the set of MBS services of interest sorted by decreasing order of interest.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.9.4.2, Initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 5.9.4.5, Setting of the contents of MBS Interest Indication
results.model_answer: A UE in RRC_CONNECTED shall send MBSInterestIndication when it is configured with mbs-InterestIndicationConfig and an indication is triggered, including upon configuration/reconfiguration of that indication, a change in the UE’s set of MBS frequencies of interest, or a change in MBS reception priority. If the set of MBS frequencies of interest is non-empty, the message shall include mbs-FreqList-r17 containing the MBS frequencies of interest (NR-ARFCNs). It also includes mbs-Priority-r17 when MBS reception is prioritized over unicast reception.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.7.3.1 (MBS interest indication procedure—General), and the MBSInterestIndication-r17 / MBSInterestIndication-r17-IEs definitions in clause 6.2.2.

results.question: When does the network initiate the RRC reconfiguration procedure for a reconfigurationWithSync in the masterCellGroup, and what is a prerequisite for a UE to initiate the RRC connection re-establishment procedure?
results.reference: The network initiates the RRC reconfiguration procedure for a reconfigurationWithSync in the masterCellGroup only when AS security has been activated, and SRB2 with at least one DRB or multicast MRB or, for IAB, SRB2, are setup and not suspended (Clause_5_3_5_2). A UE in RRC_CONNECTED, for which AS security has been activated with SRB2 and at least one DRB/multicast MRB setup or, for IAB, SRB2, may initiate the RRC connection re-establishment procedure in order to continue the RRC connection (Clause_5_3_7_1).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.5.2, Initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 5.3.7.1, General RRCReestablishmentRequest RRCReestablishment RRCReestablishmentComplete RRCReestablishmentRequest RRCSetup RRCSetupComplete
results.model_answer: The network initiates RRC reconfiguration with reconfigurationWithSync in the masterCellGroup when it needs the UE to perform handover (i.e., synchronise to a target MCG/PCell configuration). A UE may initiate RRC connection re-establishment only if AS security has been activated.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clauses 5.3.5.1 (RRC reconfiguration, including handover via RRCReconfiguration/reconfigurationWithSync) and 5.3.7.1 (RRC connection re-establishment; AS security activation prerequisite).

results.question: What parameters define the entering and leaving conditions for Event A1, and what are the corresponding conditions for Event S1?
results.reference: For Event A1, Ms is the measurement result of the serving cell, Hys is the hysteresis parameter, and Thresh is the threshold parameter. The entering condition is Ms - Hys > Thresh, and the leaving condition is Ms + Hys < Thresh. For Event S1, the entering condition is satisfied when condition S1-1 is fulfilled, and the leaving condition is satisfied when condition S1-2 is fulfilled.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.4.2, Event A1 (Serving becomes better than threshold); TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.10.4.2, Event S1 (Serving becomes better than threshold)
results.model_answer: Event A1 is defined by the serving-cell measurement result Ms, hysteresis Hys, threshold Thresh (a1-Threshold), and timeToTrigger for qualification: entering when Ms − Hys > Thresh; leaving when Ms + Hys < Thresh. Event S1 uses the sidelink measurement result MSL, Hys, threshold Thresh (s1-Threshold), and timeToTrigger: entering when MSL − Hys > Thresh; leaving when MSL + Hys < Thresh.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.4 (event-triggered measurement reporting / event triggering criteria), Event A1 and sidelink Event S1 definitions; corresponding ReportConfigNR/EventA1 and SL-EventTriggerConfig/EventS1 ASN.1 IEs define a1-Threshold, s1-Threshold, hysteresis and timeToTrigger.

results.question: For an NR cell measurement triggered by an eventA3 report, what quantity does the UE use to sort the cell measurement results, and what is the condition for considering a serving cell associated with a different measObjectNR as a neighbouring cell?
results.reference: For an NR cell with reportType set to eventTriggered, the UE considers the quantity used in the aN-Offset (for eventA3) as the sorting quantity. Furthermore, if eventA3 is configured and a serving cell is associated with a measObjectNR and neighbours are associated with another measObjectNR, the UE considers any serving cell associated with the other measObjectNR to be a neighbouring cell as well.
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.5.3, Sorting of cell measurement results; TS 24.301, Clause 5.5.4.1, General
results.model_answer: The UE sorts the reported cell measurement results in descending order of the measurement quantity used for the event evaluation (the A3 triggering quantity: RSRP, RSRQ, or SINR, as applicable). A serving cell associated with another measObjectNR is considered a neighbouring cell only if that measObjectNR is on the same frequency as the measObjectNR being evaluated (i.e. same SSB frequency and subcarrier spacing).
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.5.5.1 (Measurement reporting — General), together with the event-A3 reporting rules in clause 5.5.5.2 (Event-triggered reporting).

results.question: What is the purpose of the UuMessageTransferSidelink procedure, and what specific action does the L2 U2N Relay UE take upon receiving a Paging message for the connected Remote UE?
results.reference: The purpose of the UuMessageTransferSidelink procedure is to transfer Paging message and System Information from the L2 U2N Relay UE to the L2 U2N Remote UE in RRC_IDLE/RRC_INACTIVE (Clause_5_8_9_9_1). The L2 U2N Relay UE initiates the Uu message transfer procedure upon receiving a Paging message related to the connected L2 U2N Remote UE from the network, and it shall include sl-PagingDelivery in the UuMessageTransferSidelink message if the Paging message contains the associated ue-Identity of the L2 U2N Remote UE (Clause_5_8_9_9_2).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.9.9.1, General UuMessageTransferSidelink; TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.9.9.2, Actions related to transmission of UuMessageTransferSidelink message
results.model_answer: The UuMessageTransferSidelink procedure transfers Uu RRC messages between the network and a Remote UE through an L2 U2N Relay UE. When the relay receives a Paging message for a connected Remote UE, it forwards the Paging message to that Remote UE in a UuMessageTransferSidelink message over PC5.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause "UuMessageTransferSidelink" (under clause 5.7, Other procedures), including the L2 U2N Relay UE reception behaviour for Paging addressed to a connected Remote UE.

results.question: Under what condition can a UE initiate the sidelink UE capability transfer procedure, and what is the general purpose of the network-initiated UE capability enquiry procedure?
results.reference: A UE may initiate the sidelink UE capability transfer procedure upon indication from upper layers when it needs (additional) UE radio access capability information (Clause_5_8_9_2_2). The network initiates the UE capability enquiry procedure to a UE in RRC_CONNECTED when it needs (additional) UE radio access capability information (Clause_5_6_1_2).
results.gold_evidence: TS 24.301, Clause 5.8.9.2.2, Initiation; TS 24.301, Clause 5.6.1.2, Initiation
results.model_answer: A UE may initiate sidelink UE capability transfer when it is in RRC_CONNECTED and has a change in its sidelink UE capabilities. The network-initiated UE capability enquiry procedure is used to obtain/retrieve the UE's radio-access capability information so the network can determine the UE features and configurations it supports.
results.evidence: 3GPP TS 38.331, clause 5.10 (Sidelink UE capability transfer; UE-initiated reporting following a sidelink capability change in RRC_CONNECTED) and clause 5.6.2.1 (UE capability enquiry—network retrieval of UE capabilities).

results.question: Under what conditions does a UE initiate the RRC connection re-establishment procedure, and what is one specific action it takes upon selecting a suitable cell while timer T311 is running?
results.reference: The UE initiates the RRC connection re-establishment procedure upon detecting radio link failure of the MCG and t316 is not configured, among other conditions. Upon selecting a suitable NR cell while timer T311 is running, the UE stops timer T311.
